macro.text: Nasdaq-100 futures −1.5%, S&P −0.7%, Dow −0.1% as Nvidia leads AI stocks lower; Micron, Intel and AMD each −5%+ premarket after the indexes' best week since August.
Bessent calls for a 'dramatic shakeup' at Nvidia: look outside for the next CEO and scrutinize export-control compliance. NVDA −3.5% premarket; reports Tue after the close.
10-year 5.145%, 30-year 5.476%, little changed; dollar index ~103.4. Warsh speaks at noon ET; a December hike was fully priced after Friday's PPI.
Two tankers reportedly struck mines in Hormuz, yet Brent is 94.68 (−1.2%) and WTI 87.82 (−0.8%) on the price feed as the IEA's surplus view dominates.
China's October industrial output, retail sales and investment all missed; Japan's Q3 GDP fell 0.1% annualized vs +0.3% expected.
China confirms a Xi-Trump-Putin summit (tariffs, Iran, Ukraine on the agenda); Sen. Cantwell urges Lutnick to stop AI chip sales to China before the Xi meeting.

briefs.read: Risk-off in tech: QQQ −1.3%, SPY −0.6%, IWM −0.5% premarket; VIX 20.56. Chips de-risk again (SMH −3.9%) before Nvidia reports Tue after the close. Only U.S. red event: Warsh at 12:00 PM ET (10-year ~5.15%, December hike priced). Let SMH and QQQ set a 15-minute range first; anything open at noon carries Warsh risk.

briefs.flowNote: Money is moving into defensives and out of chips and growth. Health care (XLV +1.0% premarket, +6.9% a month), staples (XLP +0.6%), utilities and financials (+0.2% each) are the only gainers, helped by Lilly's deal and Humana's upgrade. Semiconductors (SMH −3.9%), high-growth tech (ARKK −2.5%), technology (XLK −2.0%) and software (IGV −1.1%) are losing it as chips de-risk before Nvidia's report and yields hold near 5.15% before Warsh. Energy (XLE −0.4%) gives back a little with Brent −1.2%.

bigPicture: The AI chip group is being de-risked before Nvidia's first report under interim CEO Kress (Tue after the close): SMH fell 3.0% Friday and is −3.9% premarket, with no new company numbers behind most of the moves.
Rates still set the ceiling: the 10-year near 5.15% and 30-year near 5.48% with a December hike fully priced leave leveraged and long-duration AI names (CRWV −6.9%, ORCL −3.2%) as the funding source.
Money hides in steady earners: health care, staples, utilities and financials are the only sectors up premarket and the leaders over a month.
Global growth adds to the caution: China's October output, retail sales and investment all missed, and Japan's Q3 GDP shrank 0.1% annualized against a 0.3% gain expected.
snapshot.takeaway: This is a pre-Nvidia de-risking day with Warsh at noon: chips are gapping lower on positioning, not new numbers, and defensives are taking the money. The first hour's read is the premarket levels (NVDA 155.60 below, 158.39 above); a morning break is not settled until Warsh has spoken.

macro.text: Nvidia fallout: Commerce targets loophole for China's use of overseas data centers; chip losses deepen.
Fed Chair Warsh stresses AI's importance to the economy but says it could 'disappoint'; no comment on rates.
U.S. crude falls to about $85 on recovering Middle East exports; WTI closed 85.30 (−3.7%).
Nasdaq 100 sinks 2.7% in gloomy start to pivotal week for AI trade; VIX 22.91.

Chase, Bank of America and other big-bank customers report online-banking outages after the close.

briefs.read: The pre-Nvidia chip de-risking call held and got worse: the 9:45 bounce (QQQ 672.14, NVDA 163.00) was the high, SPY broke its 30-min range down at 10:05 and lows came late (QQQ 660.48 at 3:35). Chips −5.1%, deepened by the midday Commerce China report and Warsh's AI warning. Setups bounced to gap edges, then puts sides all day; HUM swing confirmed. Retail sales 8:30 AM, Nvidia after the close.
